headline: 18 killed as US and Iran exchange massive strikes in Middle East
summary: The worst barrage since July has left dozens injured and raised fears of a full-scale war, with targets hit across Iran, Iraq, Jordan, and Kuwait.
details: The United States and Iran have engaged in their most significant exchange of fire since July, with Washington targeting Iran's southern coast and Tehran striking US bases across the Middle East. Iran's health minister reported 18 people killed and 108 injured in the latest wave of US attacks.

headline_marked: ACC [[launches probe against Asif Mahmud]] and 3 officials over corruption
headline: ACC launches probe against Asif Mahmud and 3 officials over corruption
summary: Former interim government adviser Asif Mahmud is the first from the interim administration to face an ACC inquiry into alleged irregularities at the Ministry of Youth and Sports.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has launched an investigation into alleged corruption and irregularities at the Ministry of Youth and Sports, naming four officials including former interim government adviser Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan.

ACC Deputy Director Akhtarul Islam stated that the probe was prompted by a complaint and preliminary evidence. Asif Mahmud is the first former interim government adviser to be subject to such an inquiry.

The allegations involve corruption in recruitment, promotions, appointments, and transfers, as well as procurement through a syndicate. Three other officials—former ministry secretary Md Mahbub-ul-Alam, former joint secretary Sheikh Mohammad Zobayer Hossain, and deputy secretary Md Masum Ahmed—are also under investigation.

Specific claims include the alleged collection of Tk 76 lakh for the transfer of 38 upazila youth development officers, Tk 1.5 crore for promoting 150 assistant officers, and Tk 2 crore for securing preferred postings after promotion.
Asif Mahmud, spokesperson of the National Citizen Party, has denied all allegations, calling them politically motivated.

He has given the ACC a 24-hour ultimatum to apologize for defaming him, warning that he would serve a legal notice if they fail to do so, while maintaining he is ready to cooperate with any lawful inquiry.
caption:
A former interim government adviser is under investigation for corruption. The ACC is probing alleged bribes for postings and promotions.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has launched an investigation into alleged corruption and irregularities at the Ministry of Youth and Sports, naming four officials including former interim government adviser Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan.

ACC Deputy Director Akhtarul Islam stated that the probe was prompted by a complaint and preliminary evidence. Asif Mahmud is the first former interim government adviser to be subject to such an inquiry.

The allegations involve corruption in recruitment, promotions, appointments, and transfers, as well as procurement through a syndicate. Three other officials—former ministry secretary Md Mahbub-ul-Alam, former joint secretary Sheikh Mohammad Zobayer Hossain, and deputy secretary Md Masum Ahmed—are also under investigation.

Specific claims include the alleged collection of Tk 76 lakh for the transfer of 38 upazila youth development officers, Tk 1.5 crore for promoting 150 assistant officers, and Tk 2 crore for securing preferred postings after promotion.

Asif Mahmud, spokesperson of the National Citizen Party, has denied all allegations, calling them politically motivated.

He has given the ACC a 24-hour ultimatum to apologize for defaming him, warning that he would serve a legal notice if they fail to do so, while maintaining he is ready to cooperate with any lawful inquiry.
